official.deadline_central_display: 14 September 2026 at 23:59 (Europe/Paris) - the closing published on the 2026/27 call page; the live AUF FOAD catalogue separately displayed 11 October 2026 as the closing for January 2027-intake sessions
official.deadline_note: The call page sets two intake-specific deadlines: 9 June 2026 for programmes starting September/October 2026 and 14 September 2026 (23:59 Europe/Paris) for programmes starting January/February 2027. On 10 October 2026 the live catalogue (formations.auf.org) displayed 'Les dates de cloture des candidatures : 11 octobre 2026 pour la rentree universitaire de janvier 2027', i.e. a later, session-level date for the January 2027 intake that differs from the call page's 14 September closing.
official.status_note: The AUF 'Appels a propositions' platform lists this 2026/27 FOAD diplômant call with a 'Closed' marker and states closing 14 September 2026 at 23:59 (Europe/Paris); the final stated closing date has passed as of the verification date, although the live catalogue still displayed January 2027-intake sessions with a closing of 11 October 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: 'Une allocation de mobilite virtuelle internationale sous forme d'une prise en charge partielle des frais d'inscription pour les etudiants les plus meritants ou ayant des ressources limitees' - a virtual international mobility allowance in the form of PARTIAL coverage of enrolment fees for the most meritorious or resource-limited students. No amount, percentage or cap is published.
benefits: Une allocation de mobilite virtuelle internationale sous forme d'une prise en charge partielle des frais d'inscription pour les etudiants les plus meritants ou ayant des ressources limitees (virtual international mobility allowance as partial enrolment-fee coverage)

Un accompagnement depuis la candidature jusqu'a l'obtention du diplome en passant par le suivi de la formation et l'organisation des examens et soutenances (support from application to the diploma, including course follow-up and the organisation of exams and defences)
Un acces gratuit aux implantations de l'AUF partout dans le monde durant tout le processus de la formation (free access to AUF offices worldwide throughout the training process)
eligibility: Vous etes etudiant.e Francophone - the call is addressed to francophone students
The degree is obtained 'sans quitter votre pays de residence' - without leaving the country of residence
The allowance targets 'les etudiants les plus meritants ou ayant des ressources limitees' - the most meritorious students or those with limited resources
Enrolment in one of the 150+ international distance degree programmes (licence to doctorat) delivered by 45+ AUF member institutions in 13 countries, per the AUF catalogue
requirements: Apply to one of the international distance degree programmes (FOAD) listed in the AUF catalogue, from licence to doctorat
Meet the entry requirements of the AUF member institution delivering the chosen programme
Submit through the AUF calls-for-applications platform before the closing date of the session for that programme
selection_criteria: Limited resources - 'ou ayant des ressources limitees'
coverage: Partial coverage of enrolment fees ('prise en charge partielle des frais d'inscription') through the virtual international mobility allowance
Free access to AUF offices (implantations) worldwide throughout the whole training process
Personalised support from the application stage to the diploma, including follow-up of the programme and organisation of exams and thesis defences
application_method: Consult the AUF catalogue of 150+ international distance degree programmes (https://l.auf.org/FOAD-FD)
Create an account on the AUF-Usagers centralised account system (via appels-propositions.auf.org) and confirm it through the link sent by e-mail
Submit the application for the chosen FOAD programme through the AUF calls-for-applications platform (eMundus)
Contact foad@auf.org for further information about the call
official.application_route: Online through the AUF calls-for-applications platform (appels-propositions.auf.org) for a session of one of the FOAD programmes in the AUF catalogue.
official.study_mode: Distance learning (FOAD - formation ouverte et a distance), 100% at a distance, without leaving the country of residence
official.citizenship_residency: Open to francophone students ('etudiant.e Francophone'); eligibility is linguistic rather than nationality-based, and the programme is designed so the degree is obtained without leaving the country of residence.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the AUF frames the call for francophone students internationally; the catalogue's programmes are international degrees delivered by AUF member institutions across 13 countries (the current catalogue lists 14 countries, 61 institutions and 249 programmes, 101 open).
official.duration: Licence, master or doctorat - the duration of the chosen programme; the AUF publishes no single duration for the scheme.
official.description: With the support of its Institut de la Formation a Distance de la Francophonie (IFIC), the Agence Universitaire de la Francophonie (AUF) supports francophone students enrolling in international distance degree programmes (FOAD) - more than 150 degree programmes from licence to doctorat offered by more than 45 AUF member institutions in 13 countries - so that they can obtain a university degree without leaving their country of residence. Support takes the form of a virtual international mobility allowance partially covering enrolment fees for the most meritorious or resource-limited students, accompaniment from the application through to the diploma, and free access to AUF offices worldwide.
official.region: International - AUF member institutions in 13 countries per the call (the current catalogue lists 14 countries and 61 institutions); AUF membership is concentrated in Africa, with a significant Arab Maghreb presence, plus Caribbean, Asia-Pacific, Middle East and other regions.
official.program_type: International distance degree programme (FOAD) with an AUF virtual international mobility allowance - partial enrolment-fee support

verification.notes: Checked the AUF calls platform call page (FR and EN versions agree), the IFIC announcement of 12 April 2026, the platform call listing (marked Closed) and the live FOAD catalogue - all on auf.org domains. Deadlines, benefits, eligibility and partial-fee coverage are published consistently; no monetary figure is published anywhere on the official pages.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a partial tuition-fee top-up rather than a scholarship: the AUF covers only part of the enrolment fees of an AUF-catalogue distance degree for francophone students it judges most meritorious or resource-limited, and it publishes no living-cost, travel or stipend support, so the rest of the budget stays with you. Applications go through the AUF's own calls platform with an AUF-Usagers account, and each programme session carries its own start month and closing time. As of 10 October 2026 the platform marks the 2026/27 call closed (final stated closing 14 September 2026, 23:59 Paris) while the live catalogue displayed 11 October 2026 as the closing for January 2027-intake sessions, so confirm the session date in the catalogue before treating the round as finished. The support also continues after admission: AUF accompanies students up to the diploma, including exam and defence organisation, with free access to its offices worldwide.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Francophone students in AUF member countries - concentrated in Africa and the Arab Maghreb - who cannot relocate, have strong academic records or limited means, and need only part of their enrolment fees covered.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm the exact programme appears in the AUF FOAD catalogue (l.auf.org/FOAD-FD) and that its session is still accepting applications before preparing anything else
Create the AUF-Usagers account early and confirm it via the e-mailed link - the calls platform requires the account before any submission
Assemble the delivering institution's admission file (diplomas, transcripts, identity documents) in parallel, since the AUF call page publishes no separate document list
Match the application to the session start month: the 2026/27 call set 9 June 2026 for September/October 2026 starts and 14 September 2026 for January/February 2027 starts, all at 23:59 Europe/Paris
Build the merit-or-limited-resources argument with evidence (grades, income situation), since the allowance explicitly targets the most meritorious or resource-limited students
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a programme that is not in the AUF FOAD catalogue or not delivered by an AUF member institution - the allowance only attaches to those programmes
Missing the session-specific closing date: deadlines are tied to each programme's start month and expressed in Europe/Paris time, not the applicant's local time zone
Assuming the grant covers the whole fee - it is explicitly a partial ('partielle') coverage, so under-budgeting is the classic failure mode
An incomplete admission file for the delivering university - AUF support sits on top of the institution's own entry requirements, which still apply in full
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The remainder of the enrolment fees (coverage is explicitly partial and no percentage is published), plus all living costs, connectivity and equipment, travel, and any exam or defence-related costs - the AUF publishes no living-cost, travel or stipend support for this call.
document_audit: The call page itemises no documents, so the operative list is the delivering institution's admission requirements - obtain it from the programme's session page or the nearest AUF office

Academic documents must normally be certified copies and, for francophone institutions, usable in French - verify the institution's language of instruction before paying for translations or apostilles
Keep the AUF-Usagers account confirmation e-mail: submission, tracking and any follow-up of the file all happen inside that same platform
alerts: Timing trap: the platform marked the 2026/27 call closed on 14 September 2026, yet the live catalogue showed 11 October 2026 as the January 2027-intake closing - treat the catalogue session date as the operative one and confirm with foad@auf.org
Deadlines close at 23:59 Europe/Paris, which is earlier the same calendar day in African time zones
This is not full funding and carries no stipend - never budget it as a living allowance
The AUF does not publish how many allowances exist per cohort, so selection is competitive and not guaranteed even for eligible applicants
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create and confirm an AUF-Usagers account on the AUF calls platform, open the session page of the chosen FOAD programme, submit the application together with the institution's admission file online before that session's closing (23:59 Europe/Paris), then follow up through foad@auf.org or the nearest AUF office.
